units.title: 四级选词：肥皂膜中的光色与排液
units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose an unchanged word from the shared fifteen-word bank for each gap. Each word may be used at most once; five are not needed.

materials.title: Colours on a Moving Film
materials.text:
A classroom video followed a sheet of soap solution stretched across a ring. The liquid formed a thin ____1____, a layer with two surfaces. The underlying solution could be ____2____, without an inherent strong hue, while the layer still displayed moving bands of colour under the stated lighting.

Light returning from the two boundaries could combine through ____3____. Different wavelengths were strengthened or weakened under the conditions described. The tutor distinguished this process from merely adding blue pigment to the solution. The layer’s ____4____, the distance across it, influenced which colours appeared.

Liquid moving down through the layer was described as ____5____, loss through flow rather than direct conversion into vapour. ____6____ supplied the downward pull associated with this movement. The video also allowed for ____7____, liquid becoming vapour at the surface. These were different ways for the liquid layer to become thinner.

A ____8____ enclosed gas inside a liquid boundary. A collection of many such gas-filled cells was ____9____. The class did not treat one spherical object and a whole mass of cells as the same structural level.

Eventually, a ____10____ broke the continuity of the layer. After that event, the previous intact sheet could no longer be treated as unchanged. The lesson used an already recorded demonstration, not a request to handle chemicals. It connected a visible pattern with layer structure and the processes changing it. A colourful surface was evidence to interpret, rather than proof that the solution itself had acquired every colour seen in the film.

questions.prompt: Colours on a Moving Film: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: thin layer two surfaces定义film薄膜。foam多泡整体、bubble封气单泡不是环上单片液层，其他不合。

questions.prompt: Colours on a Moving Film: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: without inherent strong hue定义colourless无色。opaque不透明说透光非本色，elastic弹性不表色性质。

questions.prompt: Colours on a Moving Film: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: boundary light combine wavelengths strengthened weakened定义interference干涉。reflection反射只是返光而非两束叠加强弱机制，其他不合。

questions.prompt: Colours on a Moving Film: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: distance across layer定义thickness厚度。pressure压强、gravity重力非跨膜空间距离。

questions.prompt: Colours on a Moving Film: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: loss through liquid flow defines drainage排液。evaporation变汽下段对照，rupture破裂是后段连续性断开。

questions.prompt: Colours on a Moving Film: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: downward pull定义gravity重力。pressure压强不特指向下吸引，reflection光过程非液下移原因名。

questions.prompt: Colours on a Moving Film: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: liquid becoming vapour定义evaporation蒸发。drainage流失非相变，reflection返光不是水成汽。

questions.prompt: Colours on a Moving Film: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: enclosed gas liquid boundary定义bubble气泡。foam泡集不是单封气单元，film平片不必包气。

questions.prompt: Colours on a Moving Film: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: many gas-filled cells defines foam泡沫。bubble单泡非集体，pressure压强非多泡材料结构。

questions.prompt: Colours on a Moving Film: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: break continuity defines rupture破裂。drainage流动可在膜仍完整时发生，reflection光返不破结构。

materials.title: A Magnet That Could Be Switched
materials.text:
A science museum used an enclosed model to explain an electromagnet. Wire wound into repeated turns formed a ____1____. A piece of iron placed inside it acted as the ____2____, the central material that affected the magnetic arrangement. The display identified these parts rather than calling every metal object a magnet.

A ____3____ connected or interrupted the intended electrical path. When the ____4____ was complete under the model’s conditions, charges could circulate through that path. Their rate of flow was ____5____, distinct from the quantity used to describe an electrical potential difference.

The wire’s outer covering was ____6____, arranged to prevent unintended electrical contact between neighbouring turns. Its metal interior was ____7____, allowing charge to move through the intended route. These properties belonged to different parts of the same wire and were not contradictory descriptions.

The model produced a magnetic ____8____, the region-related physical condition through which magnetic interactions were described. Its two ____9____ were labelled north and south under the display’s convention. The tutor did not equate a magnetic pole with an isolated electrical charge.

Under the demonstrated conditions, the device could ____10____ suitable iron pieces, drawing them towards it. That observation was not a claim that every metal or every object would respond in the same way. The museum showed the effect changing with the model’s electrical state and distinguished it from a magnet intended to retain its properties without an ongoing supply. Visitors interpreted the enclosed demonstration; no construction or handling of an electrical device was required.

questions.prompt: A Magnet That Could Be Switched: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: wire repeated turns定义coil线圈。series串联安排非卷绕部件，circuit整体电路不专绕线。

questions.prompt: A Magnet That Could Be Switched: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: central iron material定义core铁芯。poles两磁极不是中部材料，resistance性质非部件。

questions.prompt: A Magnet That Could Be Switched: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: connect interrupt path定义switch开关。coil绕线、core芯不命名控制通断器件。

questions.prompt: A Magnet That Could Be Switched: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: complete path charges circulate定义circuit电路。field磁场非闭合导电路线，series串联仅连接方式。

questions.prompt: A Magnet That Could Be Switched: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: charge flow rate定义current电流。voltage电势差下句明确不同，resistance电阻非电荷单位时间流量。

questions.prompt: A Magnet That Could Be Switched: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: cover prevents unintended contact定义insulated绝缘。conducting导电相反且内层下空，permanent持久不说明阻断接触。

questions.prompt: A Magnet That Could Be Switched: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: metal allows charge movement定义conducting导电。insulated绝缘表层而非芯层，static静态不表导电。

questions.prompt: A Magnet That Could Be Switched: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: magnetic interaction physical condition定义field场。current电荷流、resistance电阻非磁相互作用的场名称。

questions.prompt: A Magnet That Could Be Switched: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: north south pair定义poles磁极。core中心单件、series连接方式不是南北两端角色。

questions.prompt: A Magnet That Could Be Switched: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: draw towards defines attract吸引。其他候选无相应原形动作，conducting分词、permanent形容性质不做could后动词。

materials.title: A Walk Made from Strings
materials.text:
A theatre workshop examined a marionette used in a short walking scene. The puppet was ____1____, hanging from strings rather than standing on the table under its own power. The bar in the performer’s hand provided a means of ____2____ over selected movements. It did not turn every string movement into an identical action of the puppet.

A wooden arm was a ____3____, one of the body’s projecting members. The bending connection in the middle of that arm represented an ____4____. One connection used a ____5____, a fitting that allowed bending mainly about a single axis under this design.

The point about which a piece turned was its ____6____. Movement around it was ____7____. The tutor contrasted that with ____8____, movement of a piece from place to place without the same turning in the simplified example. A whole puppet action could combine these kinds of movement.

The strings carried ____9____, the pulling force transmitted through them. A line left ____10____ hung loose and could fail to pass on a small change from the control bar immediately. The performer therefore attended to the relation between hand, line and body, not only the intended gesture.

The workshop used the particular puppet’s construction to explain its actions. Other designs could use different connections and controls. A convincing walk emerged from coordinated changes rather than from one magic string labelled walking. The recorded example was complete enough to compare the stated mechanical roles without requiring learners to inspect a missing performance video.

questions.prompt: A Walk Made from Strings: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: hanging strings defines suspended悬挂。rigid刚性不说明空中挂，slack松弛非偶整体悬起。

questions.prompt: A Walk Made from Strings: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: performer bar means influence selected movement定义control控制。support支撑可承重但此处后接over selected movements命名操控，costume服装无关。

questions.prompt: A Walk Made from Strings: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: body projecting member arm定义limb肢。elbow肘部、hinge铰链不同结构层。

questions.prompt: A Walk Made from Strings: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: arm middle bending connection且an后定义elbow肘。hinge机械铰链器件非仿人体肘部名称，limb为整个肢体而不是中部关节。

questions.prompt: A Walk Made from Strings: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: fitting single-axis bend定义hinge铰链。elbow仿人体肘部位置不具体命名该机械器件，pivot转点非装配件。

questions.prompt: A Walk Made from Strings: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: point about which turns定义pivot枢点。rotation转动过程不指支点位置，balance平衡状态异。

questions.prompt: A Walk Made from Strings: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: movement around point定义rotation旋转。translation不转地移位下空，rehearsal排练是活动非运动类型。

questions.prompt: A Walk Made from Strings: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: place to place without turning定义translation平移。rotation旋转相反，control控制不命名该位移类型。

questions.prompt: A Walk Made from Strings: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: pulling force string defines tension张力。balance力平衡不等单线拉力，support支撑功能非此物理量。

questions.prompt: A Walk Made from Strings: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: line hung loose defines slack松的。rigid硬挺相反，suspended仅被吊不说明线松，其他词不合。

units.title: 四级选词：表面上的露、霜与空气湿度
units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose an unchanged word from the shared fifteen-word bank for each gap. Each word may be used at most once; five are not needed.

materials.title: Drops on the Window
materials.text:
A school weather club compared a wet window with a frosted metal plate in prepared examples. Water in the air could exist as ____1____, its gaseous state, without being visible as separate drops. The air’s ____2____ concerned the water present in that gaseous form. The club did not use visible cloudiness as a complete measurement of it.

The temperature of a ____3____, the outer boundary of the glass or metal, could differ from the air reading taken elsewhere in the room. The tutor therefore distinguished the object being measured before comparing two numbers. A familiar place name did not make all nearby objects equally warm.

Air described as ____4____ had reached the relevant limit for water vapour under the stated conditions. Cooling could lead to ____5____, the change from gas to liquid. The resulting small drops on the example window were ____6____. They were not necessarily rain that had fallen from a cloud.

On the prepared colder plate, ____7____ named the direct change from vapour to solid ice. The ice crystals formed there were ____8____. The club kept that mechanism separate from freezing already existing liquid drops.

When conditions changed, liquid water could ____9____, entering the air as vapour again. The measured ____10____ described how hot or cold the named object or air sample was. The lesson joined these quantities and processes without treating them as interchangeable words. It explained the supplied observations; it did not claim that one window’s condition could serve as a complete forecast for the surrounding town.

questions.prompt: Drops on the Window: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: gaseous water defines vapour水汽。liquid液态与气态相反，precipitation降水不是隐形气体。

questions.prompt: Drops on the Window: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: water vapour air amount/property defines humidity湿度。temperature冷热不同，radiation辐射非空气水汽量。

questions.prompt: Drops on the Window: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: outer object boundary定义surface表面。ventilation通风、liquid相态都不命名物体边界。

questions.prompt: Drops on the Window: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: relevant vapour limit defines saturated饱和。transparent透明不表容纳水汽界限，liquid不描述空气该性质。

questions.prompt: Drops on the Window: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: gas to liquid defines condensation凝结。deposition气到固下段，precipitation降落非气液相变名。

questions.prompt: Drops on the Window: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: small condensed surface drops定义dew露。frost冰晶而非液滴，precipitation来自大气降落与此表面原位不同。

questions.prompt: Drops on the Window: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: direct vapour solid defines deposition凝华。condensation气液不同，radiation能量过程不是水相变。

questions.prompt: Drops on the Window: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: formed ice crystals defines frost霜。dew液滴下文对照，liquid液态相反。

questions.prompt: Drops on the Window: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: liquid enter air vapour defines evaporate蒸发。其余多名词且不能could后作对应原形动作，deposition亦相态方向相反。

questions.prompt: Drops on the Window: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: how hot cold defines temperature温度。humidity水汽性质、ventilation气流更新不是冷热量。

units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose an unchanged word from the shared fifteen-word bank for each gap. Each word may be used at most once; five are not needed.

materials.title: Why the Blocks Stayed Together
materials.text:
An engineering museum displayed a model bridge made from shaped blocks. Its ____1____ was the curved structural form carrying forces towards its ends. The ____2____ was the part representing the roadway above. These names identified different components, even though visitors might casually call the whole object a bridge.

The blocks were mainly in ____3____ under the simplified loading, pressed together rather than pulled apart. The central top block was the ____4____, identified by its position and role in this particular arrangement. The exhibit did not claim that its name meant it alone carried every force in the bridge.

The ____5____ applied in the demonstration was the force the structure had to carry. Its path continued into the end ____6____, the solid masses receiving the arch’s thrust. A ____7____ beneath them spread forces into the supporting ground in the model’s account. Calling only the visible curve the structure would miss these necessary relationships.

Part of the force acted ____8____, pushing towards the sides rather than only straight down. The horizontal ____9____ measured the distance crossed between the stated end supports. It was not the length measured along the curved row of blocks.

During assembly, a ____10____ frame held the pieces before the complete arrangement could stand as intended. It was removed under the museum’s demonstration procedure. The class distinguished a construction stage from the completed structure and kept the model’s assumptions visible. The display illustrated a force path; it provided neither a design for a real bridge nor evidence that every curved object was automatically stable.

questions.prompt: Why the Blocks Stayed Together: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: curved structural form end force path定义arch拱。deck路面部件下空，symmetry对称性质不是结构形式。

questions.prompt: Why the Blocks Stayed Together: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: roadway part defines deck桥面。arch拱承担结构非路面层，foundation地基在下不同。

questions.prompt: Why the Blocks Stayed Together: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: pressed not pulled defines compression受压。load载荷是外加力非内压状态，mortar砂浆材料非力学状态。

questions.prompt: Why the Blocks Stayed Together: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: central top arch block定义keystone拱顶石。foundation基础、abutments桥台位置不同，其他不合。

questions.prompt: Why the Blocks Stayed Together: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: applied force carried defines load载荷。compression压应力模式不命名外加物作用，span尺寸非力。

questions.prompt: Why the Blocks Stayed Together: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: end solid masses receive thrust定义abutments桥台。tensile意为受拉的不能命名桥台实物；其他不合。

questions.prompt: Why the Blocks Stayed Together: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: beneath end masses spreads ground forces定义foundation基础。deck上面路面相反，keystone顶部非地基。

questions.prompt: Why the Blocks Stayed Together: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: push sides not only down定义outward向外。vertical垂直与侧向对照，curved形状不作方向副词。

questions.prompt: Why the Blocks Stayed Together: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: horizontal distance crossed ends定义span跨度。symmetry对称、load外力不指距离，其他不合。

questions.prompt: Why the Blocks Stayed Together: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: assembly frame later removed defines temporary临时的。vertical可能姿态但不表阶段性用途，curved形状不说明拆除角色。

materials.title: The Rectangle Became a Trapezoid
materials.text:
A media class used a prepared projector demonstration. Light passed through a ____1____, the optical component forming the projected image. The receiving ____2____ was a flat surface chosen for viewing. The tutor kept this surface separate from the source slide shown by the computer.

When the projector was not square to the surface, a rectangle could appear as a ____3____, with one pair of sides parallel and the other pair not. The resulting ____4____ concerned a change in shape rather than a different story in the slide. The familiar term ____5____ was used for this particular tapering effect in projection.

The image’s ____6____ ratio described its width in relation to its height. Enlarging it without preserving that relationship could make familiar objects seem stretched. A ____7____ adjustment changed magnification through the optical arrangement. It was different from moving the whole device sideways.

The class adjusted ____8____ to make details sharp at the receiving surface. A blurred letter and a geometrically stretched letter were different problems, even when a quick viewer described both as a bad picture.

A ____9____ ran between opposite corners of the image. Its length was one way of reporting size, not the same as width alone. The ____10____ concerned the available detail represented by the image system, rather than merely the area covered on the wall. Making a picture larger did not automatically add missing detail. The lesson supplied all geometric descriptions and did not depend on a hidden slide or an unavailable photograph.

questions.prompt: The Rectangle Became a Trapezoid: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: optical component image forms定义lens透镜。screen接收面非折光成像部件，focus调清晰状态非器件。

questions.prompt: The Rectangle Became a Trapezoid: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: receiving viewing surface定义screen屏幕。centre中心位置、offset偏移量不是接光平面。

questions.prompt: The Rectangle Became a Trapezoid: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: one pair parallel other not定义trapezoid梯形。diagonal对角线不是四边图形，keystone为效果名下空。

questions.prompt: The Rectangle Became a Trapezoid: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: change shape defines distortion畸变。contrast明暗差不是几何变形，resolution细节能力非形变。

questions.prompt: The Rectangle Became a Trapezoid: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: tapering projection term定义keystone梯形失真。distortion泛变形已上空，zoom缩放不特指斜投上窄下宽。

questions.prompt: The Rectangle Became a Trapezoid: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: width height aspect ratio宽高比。contrast ratio明暗对比非几何宽高，其他候选不命名这比值。

questions.prompt: The Rectangle Became a Trapezoid: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: optical magnification adjustment定义zoom变焦。focus调清楚非放大倍数，offset移位非同中心变倍。

questions.prompt: The Rectangle Became a Trapezoid: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: make detail sharp defines focus对焦。contrast调明暗不直接命名焦面清晰操作，zoom放大未必清楚。

questions.prompt: The Rectangle Became a Trapezoid: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: opposite corners line定义diagonal对角线。horizontal水平非必接对角，centre点不指线段。

questions.prompt: The Rectangle Became a Trapezoid: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: available image detail defines resolution分辨率。contrast明暗差、offset位移不度量可表细节，其他不合。

units.title: 六级选词：网络中的连接数、桥梁位置与方向
units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose an unchanged word from the shared fifteen-word bank for each gap. Each word may be used at most once; five are not needed.

materials.title: The Person with Few Connections
materials.text:
A fictional organisational study represented participants as ____1____ in a network. Recorded relationships became ____2____, the links connecting them. The analysts stated what counted as a relationship rather than treating every possible kind of acquaintance as the same observation. A diagram could otherwise conceal a substantial decision about what had been included.

The number of links incident on a participant was one definition of ____3____. A person with only a few contacts under that measure could still occupy a position between otherwise separated groups. Under a suitable shortest-route definition, ____4____ described that brokerage-related position. The two measures asked different questions and could rank the same people differently.

A ____5____ consisted of a sequence of connected links leading from one node to another. Which routes were available depended on the recorded network. A person absent from the dataset did not become incapable of social contact simply because the representation had no node for them.

The study used a ____6____ network where a relationship had an orientation from sender to receiver. A ____7____ link involved a corresponding relation in the reverse direction. Neither property could be inferred merely from two names appearing near each other on the page.

A ____8____ network assigned numerical values to links according to a stated rule. Those values could represent frequency, cost or another specified quantity, so a large number did not automatically mean a close friendship.

Network ____9____ compared recorded connections with the relevant possible connections under the chosen convention. The broader label ____10____ covered measures of positional importance, whose meaning depended on the question. The report did not identify one universally influential person by decorating a graph with a single ranking. It linked each result to relation definition, coverage and the particular structural property measured.

questions.prompt: The Person with Few Connections: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: participants represented network entities定义nodes节点。edges连接关系不同，path多边路线非每个人实体。

questions.prompt: The Person with Few Connections: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: links connecting nodes定义edges边。nodes为人单位，degree计连接数量不是连接本体。

questions.prompt: The Person with Few Connections: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: number incident links定义degree度。density全网连接比例后段，centrality泛位置重要性不特指该计数。

questions.prompt: The Person with Few Connections: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: shortest routes brokerage定义betweenness中介中心性。degree连接数不保证居间，robustness抗扰性非中转位置量。

questions.prompt: The Person with Few Connections: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: sequence connected links between nodes定义path路径。edges单边可构路但不是序列全称，centrality位置量非通行链。

questions.prompt: The Person with Few Connections: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: relation sender receiver orientation定义directed有向。weighted数值权重非方向，isolated孤立无连不表示边有向。

questions.prompt: The Person with Few Connections: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: corresponding reverse relation定义reciprocal互惠的。directed只定方向未必双向，withdrawn撤回不命名逆向相应连接。

questions.prompt: The Person with Few Connections: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: numerical link values定义weighted加权。directed方向不等数值，whole整体不说明权重。

questions.prompt: The Person with Few Connections: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: recorded vs possible connections定义density密度。degree单节点连接数，robustness抗破坏性质不指全网边比例。

questions.prompt: The Person with Few Connections: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: broader positional importance label定义centrality中心性。betweenness其一具体量，within介词不名测量类，其他不合。

units.title: 六级选词：中介分析中的路径与因果假设
units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose an unchanged word from the shared fifteen-word bank for each gap. Each word may be used at most once; five are not needed.

materials.title: The Route an Effect Might Take
materials.text:
A fictional methods class considered whether a training programme changed performance partly by changing confidence. Programme participation was the ____1____ whose effect was being investigated. Later performance was the ____2____. Confidence was proposed as a ____3____, an intervening variable on a possible causal route, rather than merely another name for the final performance measure.

The class distinguished an ____4____ effect, operating through the stated intervening route, from a ____5____ effect defined as bypassing it under the chosen framework. Combining these components into a ____6____ effect required the appropriate definitions and conditions. The tutor did not assume that a simple sum was justified under every model, interaction or scale.

A statistical ____7____ between confidence and performance was evidence of a relationship in the records. It did not by itself establish that intervening on confidence would produce the observed performance difference. An omitted cause influencing both could create ____8____, a mixing of influences that complicated the proposed causal interpretation.

Even if programme offers had been assigned by chance, the intervening confidence level had not necessarily been assigned in the same way. The class therefore examined assumptions needed for ____9____, connecting the causal quantities of interest with what the observed data and design could determine. Random allocation at one stage was not a universal guarantee for every later pathway claim.

A ____10____ analysis examined how conclusions could change when an assumption was varied within the stated exercise. It did not transform an unknown influence into an observed fact. The final report separated the proposed mechanism, the measured relations and the assumptions supporting a causal account. It allowed a pathway hypothesis to guide investigation without presenting every intermediate correlation as proof of how the programme worked.

materials.title: Two Sounds, One Category?
materials.text:
A fictional phonology workshop compared two speech sounds in a carefully supplied dataset. The broad category proposed to distinguish words was a ____1____. Sounds treated as conditioned realisations of that category were ____2____. This was an analysis of a particular language pattern, not a claim that two physically different sounds must always belong together in every language.

A ____3____ pair differed in one relevant sound while retaining a difference in lexical meaning under the exercise’s definitions. Such evidence could support a ____4____ between sound categories. The tutor did not infer that the absence of one such pair in a small handout proved that no contrast existed anywhere in the language.

The ____5____ of a sound concerned where it occurred across the data. Its surrounding ____6____ included the neighbouring sounds and positions relevant to the analysis. When two variants occupied non-overlapping contexts of the stated kind, the pattern was called ____7____ distribution. Even then, the proposed grouping needed to account for their relation and the coverage of the evidence, rather than follow a mechanical label alone.

The analysts distinguished an ____8____ description, concerned with the frequency and intensity of sound waves, from a decision about their role in the language’s category system. An ____9____ account described the movements and configurations of the speech organs. Neither description required that ordinary writing assign a different letter to every realisation.

The written ____10____ used specified symbols to represent the spoken material. It was not identical to the language’s everyday orthography. The workshop retained the conventions with the examples so a reader could tell whether a narrow sound difference had been represented or deliberately abstracted away. Its conclusion depended on the supplied evidence and did not turn one analysis into a universal fact about pronunciation.

materials.title: A Broad Description and a Narrow Claim
materials.text:
A fictional intellectual-property seminar examined a simplified patent record. The ____1____ were the numbered statements defining the protection sought or granted in that exercise. A broad discussion elsewhere in the document did not automatically extend those statements to every interesting use of the technology.

The document’s ____2____ supplied the technical account made available to readers. One described ____3____ was a particular way of putting the idea into practice, rather than necessarily the full extent of the protection. The class therefore kept an illustrative implementation separate from the boundaries expressed in the numbered statements.

____4____ concerned whether the claimed subject matter was new against the relevant earlier material under the exercise’s rules. The ____5____ art was that earlier publicly available technical material. The separate requirement described as ____6____ addressed a further step beyond merely being new, according to the hypothetical legal framework. The lesson did not assume that every unfamiliar combination automatically met it.

____7____ concerned whether the technical teaching was sufficient for the relevant skilled reader to carry out the subject matter as required. A striking title or a desired outcome alone did not establish that the text supplied a workable teaching under the standard being discussed.

The geographical ____8____ identified the legal system in which the right and its interpretation applied. Its ____9____ specified the relevant period of protection, subject to the conditions of the exercise. The record did not portray a patent as a permanent worldwide prohibition on all related activity.

Finally, a ____10____ could authorise specified use under an agreement. The class distinguished the existence of the right from permission granted by its holder and from a conclusion about a particular act. The case was entirely hypothetical: it offered vocabulary for reading a structured legal record, not an opinion about the validity or enforcement of an actual patent.

materials.title: A Moving Shoreline and a Sediment Budget
materials.text:
A fictional coastal-science study compared surveys of a beach. Its sediment ____1____ accounted for material entering, leaving and changing storage within a stated area and period. The analysts did not confuse this accounting framework with a financial allocation for the survey team.

A ____2____ measured the rate at which sediment passed through a defined boundary. The material’s ____3____ size described the dimensions of the particles, a property relevant to how they could move. A tonne of fine material and a tonne of coarse material were not treated as dynamically identical merely because their masses matched.

Transport parallel to the coast was ____4____. Movement away from the coast was described as ____5____ under the study’s convention. These directions referred to the local shoreline arrangement, not to a universal left and right on every printed map.

____6____ removed material from a location, while ____7____ placed transported particles there. The net building up of the beach through accumulated material was ____8____. The report distinguished a local settling process from the longer-term balance of gains and losses across the specified beach section.

A surveyed ____9____ represented the cross-sectional shape of the beach from land towards water. A single mapped shoreline position did not reveal every change within that shape. The relevant water level also mattered when interpreting an apparent boundary between wet and dry ground.

Landward movement of the defined shoreline was called ____10____. That position change was not automatically equal to the amount of sediment lost from the entire system. Material could move between visible and submerged parts or across the survey boundaries. The study therefore connected line position, cross-sectional form and material accounting instead of presenting one short sequence of shoreline photographs as a complete explanation of coastal change.

materials.title: Three Copies and One Agreed Order
materials.text:
A fictional systems seminar considered several machines maintaining a shared ordered record. The machines held ____1____, copies whose update process had to be coordinated. Agreement on the relevant value and ordering was the task of ____2____ under the protocol being studied. Merely writing the same filename on three disks did not solve that problem.

A designated ____3____ proposed or coordinated updates during the stated phase. Its role did not make it incapable of failure, nor did the title alone establish that every other machine had accepted its latest proposal. The seminar traced the messages required by the actual procedure.

A ____4____ was a set large enough to meet the protocol’s specified voting requirement. It was not necessarily every machine in the deployment. The assumptions about how such sets overlapped mattered to the agreement argument. The class did not replace those conditions with the vague idea that several positive replies were always sufficient.

The record distinguished an update being ____5____ by a receiver from that update reaching the protocol’s ____6____ point. An early receipt message could report one local event without proving the global condition needed for the latter state. The precise meaning of each response was therefore part of the interface contract.

A ____7____ guarantee ruled out specified bad outcomes, such as two conflicting decisions in the model. A ____8____ property concerned eventual progress under the required conditions. Keeping a system from deciding inconsistently and ensuring that it eventually decides were different obligations.

A network ____9____ prevented some groups of machines from exchanging messages. A local ____10____ indicated that an expected event had not arrived within the chosen interval; it did not prove that a remote machine had ceased to exist. The exercise connected protocol claims with failure and timing assumptions, rather than suggesting that more copies automatically guaranteed every desired property under every communication failure.
